gen-dafont-junegull-gf-julius-sans-one: Cast-iron capitals seem to double as lowercase in Junegull, pinched at every curve and cheerfully retro. Julius Sans One, though, spreads wide gaps between open-ended letters, so paragraphs drift by lightly.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa draws every stroke at a thickness that never shifts, with wide curves and stubby ascenders under a big x-height. Long paragraphs of it read smoothly after Junegull's pinched heading.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-lexend-mega: No thick-thin flicker anywhere in Junegull, just friendly retro letters. Lexend Mega, drawn as if with one nib and a visible gap in every c, opens up what the heading pinches shut.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta brings curves without any thinning and wide-mouthed c shapes, sitting on a big x-height with tight ascender room. Junegull's pinched heading letters close up where this body opens out.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-lexend-tera: Everything reads spaced out, letters standing like stepping stones along a single-weight, plotter-pen line with open-faced curves. Lexend Tera holds up best at a modest size, leaving Junegull's pinched heading to do the shouting.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-lexend-zetta: Retro and friendly, with pinched curves: Junegull holds its lowercase up like cast iron capitals. And where it grabs attention, Lexend Zetta lays out widely tracked, constant-width strokes that reward steady reading.
gen-dafont-kg-happy-fs-asap: Cheerful KG Happy has a dominant x-height and narrow lowercase openings, with every diagonal as sturdy as an upright. Asap's open arcs and near-capital body height loosen what the heading keeps tight.
gen-dafont-kg-happy-fs-fira-sans: KG Happy brings a youthful, handwritten bounce, with a dominant x-height and narrow openings in its lowercase. Fira Sans, with no thick-thin contrast and s curves open at both ends, gives that bounce somewhere to land.
gen-dafont-kg-happy-fs-public-sans: Youthful and cheerful, KG Happy keeps one line weight throughout, with a dominant x-height and narrow lowercase openings. It earns its keep big and brief; Public Sans handles the hefty text.
gen-dafont-kg-happy-fs-supreme: Cheerful KG Happy is all stout, closed-in letters, each diagonal as sturdy as an upright. But Supreme holds its letters open rather than curled shut, giving a crisp, heavy-looking strip of text.
